samples.summary: `rawRequest` constructs a WHATWG `Response` with a body for null-body statuses (204/205/304), which throws a raw TypeError
samples.evidence: `return new Response(Readable.toWeb(res.body) as ReadableStream<Uint8Array>, { status: res.statusCode, headers });` — the WHATWG `Response` constructor rejects a non-null body when `status` is 101/103/204/205/304 (`TypeError: Response with null body status cannot have body`). `undiciRequest` always hands back a `body` Readable, so an image endpoint answering `204 No Content` (or `304` if any intermediary adds a conditional) makes this throw a bare `TypeError` that escapes the SystemError/UserError classification the whole file is built around, and `outputError` then reports it as a user error (exit 1) with a message about `Response`. This path is now taken for *every* hop the fetch layer opaque-filters, and for every proxied+pinned hop, so it is not a rare branch.

samples.summary: Any NETWORK_ERROR on a proxied pinned hop permanently disables address pinning for the whole fetcher, not just a proxy CONNECT refusal
samples.evidence: The catch only checks `plan.pinnedThroughProxy && error instanceof SystemError && error.code === 'NETWORK_ERROR'`. `rawRequest` wraps *every* transport failure (proxy timeout, origin down, TLS error, socket reset, no route) in exactly that SystemError code, so a single transient failure sets the fetcher-scoped `pinThroughProxy = false` for the rest of the export, emits the (then incorrect) 'the proxy refused to fetch by address' warning, and silently retries by name. The condition cannot distinguish the one case the fallback is documented for from an ordinary network blip.

samples.summary: The cross-site refusal runs before port validation, so a `mode=cli` request that previously degraded to an ordinary browser login now 400s
samples.evidence: `const isCliStart = req.query?.mode === 'cli'; if (isCliStart) this.assertCliStartNotCrossSite(req);` executes before `parseCliPort`. `CliLoginConfirmMiddleware.use` (packages/backend/src/auth/cli-login-confirm.middleware.ts:78-82) explicitly calls `next()` for `mode=cli` with an unusable port precisely so it 'falls through to an ordinary browser login rather than 404-ing here', and the guard's own `else` branch then mints web state. With the new check, that same request arriving cross-site is now rejected with a BadRequestException instead of completing as a web login, contradicting the middleware's stated contract.

samples.summary: The opaque-redirect fallback silently bypasses the injected `fetch` seam and issues a real network request
samples.evidence: `if (isOpaqueRedirect(res)) { res = await rawRequest(plan.url, plan.agent, plan.headers); }` — `rawRequest` always uses undici's module-level `undiciRequest`, never `fetchImpl`. Any caller that injected `opts.fetch` (the documented test/embedding seam) loses control of the request as soon as its stub returns a status-0 response, and a real outbound request is made to `plan.url`. The comment on `isOpaqueRedirect` also asserts undici 'hands back the real response instead' of opaque-filtering `redirect: 'manual'`; undici's fetch does implement the spec's opaque-redirect filtering, so in practice every redirect hop is issued twice against the origin (once opaque-filtered and discarded, once via `rawRequest`).

samples.summary: `serverAddresses` performs a redundant DNS lookup of the API server for every image whose host is simply the server's own name
samples.evidence: `const exempt = server && mayBeServer ? await serverAddresses(server, lookup) : new Set<string>();` runs whenever `mayBeServer` is true, which includes the ordinary `sameName` case. The subsequent filter short-circuits on `sameName || ...`, so `exempt` is never consulted on that path — yet a full resolver round trip is paid per image inline in the document.

finding.summary: `rawRequest` constructs a WHATWG `Response` with a body for null-body statuses (204/205/304), which throws a raw TypeError
finding.evidence: `return new Response(Readable.toWeb(res.body) as ReadableStream<Uint8Array>, { status: res.statusCode, headers });` — the WHATWG `Response` constructor rejects a non-null body when `status` is 101/103/204/205/304 (`TypeError: Response with null body status cannot have body`). `undiciRequest` always hands back a `body` Readable, so an image endpoint answering `204 No Content` (or `304` if any intermediary adds a conditional) makes this throw a bare `TypeError` that escapes the SystemError/UserError classification the whole file is built around, and `outputError` then reports it as a user error (exit 1) with a message about `Response`. This path is now taken for *every* hop the fetch layer opaque-filters, and for every proxied+pinned hop, so it is not a rare branch.

verdict.reason: The claimed code exists verbatim: image-fetcher.ts:677-680 builds a WHATWG Response from the undici Readable body using res.statusCode with no null-body-status (204/205/304/101/103) handling, and undiciRequest (line 657) always supplies a body Readable, so such a status makes the constructor throw TypeError. The path is reachable without any guard: rawRequest is called unconditionally for pinnedThroughProxy hops (765-767) and for opaque-filtered hops (779-781), and status inspection only happens after construction (815-837). The local catch rethrows anything that is not a SystemError with code NETWORK_ERROR (800-806), so the bare TypeError escapes the file's SystemError/UserError classification and is reported by outputError (output/formatter.ts:112-118) with a code/exit class derived from an unclassified Error rather than a network/HTTP fault. No guard elsewhere prevents it; real logic/error-handling defect in the correctness lane.

mergedFrom.summary: `Sec-Fetch-Site: cross-site` refusal can break the ordinary browser sign-in when the frontend origin is cross-site from `VITE_BACKEND_API_URL`, or when the login link is reached through a cross-site redirect chain
An empty or duplicated `Sec-Fetch-Site` header is treated as an attack

finding.summary: `assertBrowserInitiated` refuses every `Sec-Fetch-Site: cross-site` start, which breaks web login entirely on any deployment where the frontend and backend are not the same site
finding.evidence: `ALLOWED_FETCH_SITES = new Set(['none','same-origin','same-site'])` and anything else throws `BadRequestException`. The web login is a plain anchor navigation from the frontend (`packages/frontend/src/components/login-form.tsx:27`, `<Link to={VITE_BACKEND_API_URL}/auth/github>` — react-router treats a cross-origin absolute URL as an external link, so the browser navigates normally and sets `Sec-Fetch-Site` relative to the frontend origin). If the frontend is served from a different registrable domain or a different scheme than the backend (e.g. a CDN/preview host in front of `api.example.com`, or a dev setup with the frontend on `localhost:5173` and `VITE_BACKEND_API_URL=http://127.0.0.1:3000` — `localhost` and `127.0.0.1` are not same-site), the header is `cross-site` and every login now 400s. Nothing in the config enforces same-site: CORS is keyed on `FRONTEND_URL` (docs/design/backend.md:604), which permits a cross-site frontend. The `SameSite=Lax` comment asserts the assumption but does not enforce it, and before this change a cross-site frontend still worked because no such check existed.

verdict.reason: The finding describes a method `assertBrowserInitiated` that refuses every cross-site start and thus 400s web login. No such method exists and the check is not applied to web logins. In packages/backend/src/auth/github-auth.guard.ts:112-113 the fetch-site check runs only behind `const isCliStart = req.query?.mode === 'cli'; if (isCliStart) this.assertCliStartNotCrossSite(req);`. The web login falls through to the unguarded `else` branch at :128-132 which mints the double-submit state and returns. `ALLOWED_FETCH_SITES` does exist at :45 as quoted, but it is only consulted inside `assertCliStartNotCrossSite` (:171-181), whose docblock at :155-163 explicitly addresses and excludes the exact deployment scenario the finding raises. The frontend link at packages/frontend/src/components/login-form.tsx:63 is `${VITE_BACKEND_API_URL}/auth/github` with no `mode=cli`, and the only producer of `mode=cli` is the CLI (packages/cli/src/commands/login.ts:262), so the web navigation never reaches the guarded branch. A regression test pins the behavior: github-auth.guard.spec.ts:206-219 asserts a browser login with `sec-fetch-site: cross-site` and no mode returns true and sets the web state cookie. No other Sec-Fetch-Site enforcement exists in the request path (cli-login-confirm.middleware.ts has none). Therefore the described breakage of web login cannot occur.
